# Task: #7213 slice 5 — burn down the subprocess-timeout allowlist for `scripts/orchestration/` (one PR)

Follow the merged pattern of slices 1–4 (#7214 `scripts/ci/`, #7215 `scripts/api/`, #7217 `scripts/ai_agent_bridge/`,
#7231 `scripts/delegate.py`): a named module-level constant per bound class, `TimeoutExpired` mapped onto each site's
EXISTING failure semantics, one test per site exercising the real code path with a monkeypatched `TimeoutExpired`.

This slice covers ONLY the 18 allowlist entries under `scripts/orchestration/`:
reaper_lifecycle.py (4) · job_host_exec.py (2) · handoff_ready.py (2) · curriculum_lifecycle_pilot.py (2) ·
task_lifecycle.py · task_closeout.py · orchestrator_control.py · integration_sweep.py ·
install_worktree_cleanup_launchd.py · install_mac_observer_launchd.py · install_archived_thread_cleanup_launchd.py ·
dispatch_settle.py (1 each). Orchestration is dispatch-adjacent silent-stall territory (the reaper, settle, and
job-host forward paths run unattended).

## Outcome
Every `scripts/orchestration/` allowlist entry is either fixed (bounded, removed from the allowlist) or explicitly
skipped with a one-line reason in the PR body. No other directories.

## Rules for values
- Grep each module for existing `timeout=` conventions FIRST and reuse them (job_host_exec has ssh transport budgets;
  reaper/launchd installers call local git/launchctl).
- Local git / launchctl / plutil: tens of seconds. ssh/remote (job_host_exec): minutes, derived from the module's own
  transport budget where one exists — never invent a competing constant.
- Map `TimeoutExpired` onto the site's existing failure shape (typed error, False/None return, warn-and-continue in
  sweeps); state the shape per site in the PR table. Fail-open vs fail-closed must MATCH the site's current posture.
- DO NOT change reaper safety predicates, settle semantics, or launchd plist contents — only bounds + mapping.

## Coordination (HARD)
Do NOT touch `thread_handoff.py`, `session_streams`, `claudex_supervisor.py`, or SessionStart hook files — they are
another lane's surfaces (none hold allowlist entries; if an edit would ripple into them, SKIP the site with reason).
